t: Maximum Subarray Sum After Multiplier — Prefix Kadane Sandwich
o: 'Understanding the problem': Pick one subarray, scale every element in it by k (multiply, or divide with truncation toward zero: floor for positives, ceiling for negatives), then report the maximum subarray sum of the resulting array. In example 1 doubling [3,4] gives best subarray 6+8=14. In example 2 dividing −3 by 2 gives −1 (ceiling), and the best subarray is just [−1]. With n up to 10⁵ we need roughly linear time; the chosen operation subarray and the answer subarray interact only through three regions: left of it, the scaled region itself, and right of it.
k: Any optimal answer subarray is either disjoint from the operated subarray or contains it entirely (partial overlaps reduce to these by shrinking the operated range).
So the answer is max over split points of (best left subarray) + (scaled sum of middle) + (best right subarray), computable with prefix Kadane arrays L and R and prefix sums.
Division here is truncation toward zero, which matches native integer division in C++/Java and needs explicit handling in Python/JS.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force Over Split Points
a.i: Enumerate every operated subarray [l, r), compute the scaled middle sum with prefix sums, and combine with precomputed best-left/best-right Kadane values. This is O(n²) pairs but establishes the decomposition that the optimal approach exploits.
s: Precompute L[i] = max subarray sum (or 0 for empty) within nums[0..i−1] and R[i] symmetrically on the suffix.
For each pair l < r, evaluate L[l] + scale(l, r) + R[r] using prefix sums for both multiply and divide variants.
a.t: O(n²) — all subarray split pairs are enumerated.

a.n: Approach 2: Linear Scan with Running Best Left Value
a.i: In the multiply candidate L[l] + k(P[r]−P[l]) + R[r], only the term L[l] − k·P[l] depends on l, so sweeping r left-to-right while maintaining bestLeft = max(L[l] − k·P[l]) evaluates all r in O(1) each. The divide candidate is analogous with prefix sums D of truncated values. This gives an O(n) solution.
s: Compute L, R (prefix/suffix Kadane allowing empty = 0) and prefix sums P (raw) and D (truncated-divided).
Sweep r from 1..n: first update bestLeftM = max(bestLeftM, L[r−1] − k·P[r−1]) and bestLeftD similarly, then consider bestLeftM + k·P[r] + R[r] and bestLeftD + D[r] + R[r].
a.t: O(n) — four linear passes plus one sweep; arithmetic per step is O(1).
a.sp: O(n) — the L, R, P, D arrays (reducible to O(1) with streaming suffix Kadane).

w: Wrap-up: Lead with the decomposition insight (disjoint-or-containing), then present the O(n) sweep as the optimal solution. Pitfalls: division rounding — Python's // floors negatives, so implement truncation explicitly; allowing empty left/right sides (initialize L/R with 0) while requiring the operated subarray to be non-empty (l < r); 64-bit intermediate sums since k·|sum| can reach ~10¹⁵·10⁵ scale within long range. Edge cases: n = 1 (must operate on the only element — covered by l=0, r=1), all-negative arrays, and k = 1 where both operations are identity. Follow-ups: multiple operations allowed, or operation on a subsequence instead of a subarray.
